title: Funeral parades and afternoon parades
summary: The band played funerals two or three times a week, marches on the way out and popular tunes returning, then parades for organizations.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Well, I'll say around... The twenties or thirties? Oh, around... I'll say around the twenties? Uh-huh. 1920s. Yeah, 1920s. Yes. And I'm saying we played funeral parades. You did play funeral parades? We played funeral parades on an average two or three times a week.
Now when did they start playing? Very long. How recently have they played funerals?
Oh, I guess that's been now over twenty years.
No funerals for the last twenty years?
You don't use them anymore. No, don't use them at all. All the organizations, you know, and... Yes. Each one had one, but a member would die, they would play some music.
They still do that over at New Orleans.

They would play such music as going out to the cemetery, funeral marches, going to the cemetery, and coming back, you had... You played regular popular music. Yes. In other words, I remember what we played very often. So glad to go and rescue you.

Bye-bye, you black boy, and all those kind of things, you know. Yes, yes. Yes. Great days. Then we made parades for the different organizations. We're parading the afternoons from three until six o'clock.
Were those on Sundays or any day in a week? Any day in a week. Almost any day. Monday was the famous... Monday and Wednesday was the regular days.
